Rashi on Gittin 39a:11:1.hebrew: אפילו תימא - הא דקתני הכא "אין מועלין בשערו", כר"מ היא:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:11:1.english: Even [if] you say - That which is taught here, "one does not commit me'ilah [misuse of consecrated property] with his hair," is [in accordance] with Rabbi Meir:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:11:2.hebrew: אשבוחי משבח - הלכך לאו כגזוז דמי, דעדיין צריך לחיבורו:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:11:2.english: It improves - Therefore, it is not considered as [already] cut, since it still needs its attachment:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:12:1.english: This teaching of Rav - [Namely, that] one who renounces ownership of his slave goes free:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:12:2.hebrew: אמר רב הכי - בתמיהה, ופריך הש"ס: ואיהו, רבי יוחנן, מי לא אמר הכי? ומאי מתמה אדרב:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:12:2.english: Did Rav say so? - [He asked this] in astonishment. And the Gemara asks: And he — [that is,] Rabbi Yochanan — did he not say so [himself]? Why, then, is he astonished at Rav?

Rashi on Gittin 39a:13:1.hebrew: לא סיימוה קמיה - למילתיה דרב כולה, אלא כרב יוסף אמרו קמיה, דלא סיים בה משמיה דרב "וצריך גט שחרור", ולא פירשו לפניו הא דאמרי' לעיל, דרב חייא בר אבין סיים בה משמיה דרב "וצריך גט שחרור":
Rashi on Gittin 39a:13:1.english: They did not conclude it before him - [meaning] Rav's entire statement; rather, they stated [it] before him like Rav Yosef, who did not conclude it in the name of Rav [with] "and he requires a bill of manumission," and they did not explain before him that which we stated above, that Rav Chiya bar Avin concluded it in the name of Rav [with] "and he requires a bill of manumission."

Rashi on Gittin 39a:15:1.hebrew: גר שמת - ואין לו יורשין, וכל נכסיו הפקר:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:15:1.english: A convert who died - and he has no heirs, and [therefore] all his property is ownerless:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:15:2.english: They acquire themselves - They have precedence over any [other] person to take possession of themselves from the ownerless property:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:15:3.english: Abba Shaul says - Minors do not have the legal capacity [lit., "a hand"] to acquire themselves:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:16:1.hebrew: מי כותב גט שחרור לאלו - מעתה להתירן בישראלית, הרי מתו בעלים:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:16:1.english: Who writes a bill of manumission for these - from now on, to permit them [to marry] an Israelite woman? Behold, [their] owners have died:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:17:1.hebrew: עבדו דגר כאשתו - כלומר, אין הפקר זה דומה להפקר מחיים, דעבד גמר "לה" "לה" מאשה — "וכתב לה ספר" (דברים כד), "או חופשה לא נתן לה" (ויקרא י״ט:כ׳) — הלכך, מחיים אין לו תקנה בלא גט כאשה; אבל הפקר שלאחר מיתה, כי היכי דאשתו משולחת בלא גט, עבדו נמי לא בעי גט:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:17:1.english: A slave of a convert is like his wife - That is to say, this [state of] ownerlessness [after the convert's death] is not similar to [declaring a slave] ownerless during [the master's] lifetime, because [the law of] a slave is derived via "to her" / "to her" from a wife — "and he writes for her a bill [of divorce]" (Deuteronomy 24), "or freedom has not been given to her" (Leviticus 19:20) — therefore, during [the master's] lifetime, he has no remedy [to become fully free] without a bill [of manumission], just like a wife; however, [regarding] ownerlessness after death, just as his wife is freed without a bill of divorce, so too his slave does not require a bill [of manumission]:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:18:1.hebrew: א"ה - ישראל שמת נמי, לא יזכו בניו בעבדיו, דהא כאשתו הם:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:18:1.english: If so - [in the case of] a Jew who died as well, his sons should not acquire his slaves, for they are like his wife:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:19:1.english: One who renounces ownership of his slave - since there is no longer an inheritance for his sons:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:19:2.hebrew: ומת - לא ליבעי גט שחרור להפקיע איסורו, דהא מית ליה, ובניו לא זכו בהן מעולם:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:19:2.english: And dies - he should not require a bill of manumission to remove his prohibition [from marrying a Jewish woman], for he [the master] has died, and his sons never acquired them:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:19:3.hebrew: אין לו תקנה - כדמפרש לקמן, דכיון דהפקירו פקע ממוניה מיניה, ואיסורא הוא דפש לבעלים עליהן, וכי מיית אין זו ירושה להוריש לבניו, הלכך אין לו מי שיתירנו בגט:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:19:3.english: There is no remedy for him - as [the Gemara] explains below, for since he renounced ownership of him, his monetary [ownership] has ceased from him, and it is [only] a prohibition that remains for the master over them; and when he dies, this is not an inheritance to bequeath to his sons — therefore, he has no one who can permit him [to marry a Jewish woman] with a bill [of manumission]:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:1:1.hebrew: הא מני ר"מ היא דאמר אין אדם מוציא דבריו - להקדש לבטלה. דתניא (ערכין דף ה.): "המעריך פחות מבן חדש, ר"מ אומר: נותן דמיו; דאדם יודע שאין ערך לפחות מבן חדש, וגמר ואמר לשם דמים". הכא נמי, יודע שאין עבד ראוי לא להקרבה ולא לבנין, וכיון דבלשון הקדש אקדשיה, גמר בדעתו להקדיש דמיו ולומר "דמיו עלי":
Rashi on Gittin 39a:1:1.english: Whose [opinion] is this? It is [that of] Rabbi Meir, who says: A person does not utter his words - [of] consecration for naught. As it is taught [in a baraita] (Arakhin 5a): "If one vows the fixed valuation of [an infant] less than a month old, Rabbi Meir says: He gives his [monetary] value, for a person knows that there is no fixed valuation for [an infant] less than a month old, and he resolved and spoke for the sake of [his monetary] value." Here too, he knows that a slave is fit neither for sacrifice nor for building [the Temple], and since he consecrated him using language of consecration, he resolved in his mind to consecrate his [monetary] value and to say, "His value is upon me":

Rashi on Gittin 39a:2:1.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא ר"מ היא - וטעמא לאו משום מקדיש סתם שיקדיש לימכר, אלא משום דאין מוציא דבריו לבטלה הוא, וכמו שאמר דמיו עלי ויש להן עליו מעות — היינו דחייב לתת דמים, דאדם יודע שאין גופו קדוש ואמר לשם דמים:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:2:1.english: Granted, if you say it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir - and the reason is not because one who consecrates without specification consecrates [the person] to be sold, rather because [a person] does not utter his words in vain, and it is as if he said that his monetary value is upon him and [the Temple treasury] has a monetary claim against him — this is why he is obligated to give [his] monetary value, for a person knows that his body cannot become consecrated, and he spoke [the vow] for the sake of [giving his] monetary value.

Rashi on Gittin 39a:3:1.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת רבנן - וטעמא משום דמקדיש סתם דבר שאין ראוי לגופו, הקדישו לדמיו לימכר:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:3:1.english: Rather, if you say [it is] the Rabbis - and the reason is because one who consecrates without specification something that is not fit for its own [sacred] use has consecrated it for its monetary value, to be sold:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:3:2.hebrew: בשלמא - בעבד איכא למימר סתמיה לדמים קאי, וה"ק: "הרי הוא קדוש לימכר". אבל בעצמו, מי איכא למימר שיהא קדוש לימכר? וכי יש דמים לבן חורין, ומה מכירה יש בו? אלא ר"מ היא, ולאו דמשמע מלתא לדמי, אלא מתוך שאינו מוציא דבריו לבטלה גמר בלבו ואמר "דמי עצמי עלי", והיינו דאמר: "הריני הקדש" — שמין אותו כעבד, ולא שימכר. וגבי עבד נמי, אין רשות הגזברין עליו, אלא מעות יש להן על הבעלים:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:3:2.english: Granted - with regard to a slave, one can say [that] by default he stands for monetary value, and this is what [the owner] is saying: "He is hereby consecrated to be sold." But with regard to himself, can one say that he is consecrated to be sold? Does a free person have a monetary value, and what sale applies to him? Rather, it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir, and [it is] not because the phrase implies monetary value, but rather, since a person does not utter his words in vain, he resolved in his mind and meant, "My own monetary value is [incumbent] upon me," and this is [the meaning of] what [the baraita] says: [When one says,] "I am hereby consecrated" — they assess him like a slave, and not that he is sold. And with regard to a slave as well, the treasurers [of the Temple] have no authority over [the slave himself], but rather they have [a claim for] money against the owner:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:4:1.english: Let us say [it is] like [a dispute of] Tannaim - [regarding] one who consecrates his slave, [whether he is] consecrated or not consecrated:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:4:2.hebrew: מועלין בשערו - דוקא נקט, ולקמיה מפרש לה:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:4:2.english: One misuses [consecrated property with] his hair - He specifically stated [his hair], and later on [the Gemara] explains it:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:5:1.hebrew: אין מעילה בקרקעות - דגמרינן מעילה "חטא" "חטא" מתרומה: מה תרומה בתלוש, אף מעילה בתלוש, במס' מעילה (דף יח:) ובת"כ:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:5:1.english: There is no misuse [of consecrated property] in land - for we derive [the laws of] misuse [through the verbal analogy of] "sin" [and] "sin" from terumah: just as terumah [applies only] to detached [produce], so too misuse [applies only] to detached [property], [as taught] in tractate Me'ilah (18b) and in Torat Kohanim:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:6:1.english: Rather, everyone [agrees that the slave is] consecrated - to be sold for his value:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:8:1.english: [It] is considered as cut - and it is not like [something] attached to the ground:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:9:1.english: There are things that are like land - [Things] attached to the ground:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:9:2.hebrew: ואינן כקרקע - דקי"ל אין נשבעין על הקרקעות, ועל גפנים הללו נשבעין בהודאת מקצת הטענה:
Rashi on Gittin 39a:9:2.english: And are not like land - For we hold that one does not take an oath regarding land, yet regarding these grapevines one does take an oath upon a partial admission of the claim:

Rashi on Gittin 39a:9:3.english: I gave you - to guard [them] on my land:

Tosafot on Gittin 39a:15:1.hebrew: קטנים כל המחזיק בהן זכה בהן - דאין להן יד לזכות בעצמן, וכן בפרק מי שמת (ב"ב קנו:) גבי פלוגתא דזכין לקטן ואין זכין לגדול. ואע"ג דאית ליה זכיה במציאה, כדאמרינן בהניזקין (לקמן גיטין נט:), היינו מדרבנן מפני דרכי שלום, והכא לא שייך ההוא טעמא. וא"ת: בפרק לולב וערבה (סוכה מו:) אמר "לא ליקני איניש לולבא לינוקא בי"ט ראשון, דינוקא מקני קני, אקנויי לא מקני", וליכא למימר דהתם בפיקח כגון צרור וזרקו אגוז ונוטלו, דהא בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כב:), בההוא עובדא דא"ל "שלוף לי מסנאי", משמע דהוה בו דעת, וקאמר התם "איכא דאמרי קטן הוה"! וי"ל דדעת אחרת מקנה אותן שאני:
Tosafot on Gittin 39a:15:1.english: Minor [slaves], anyone who takes possession of them acquires them - Because they do not have a "hand" [i.e., legal capacity] to acquire [ownership] for themselves; and similarly in the chapter [entitled] Mi SheMet (Bava Batra 156b), regarding the dispute [concerning] "one acquires for a minor and does not acquire for an adult." And even though [a minor] has [the capacity of] acquisition with respect to a found object, as we say in [the chapter entitled] HaNizakin (below, Gittin 59b), that is by rabbinic enactment for the sake of the ways of peace, and here that reason does not apply. And if you ask: In the chapter [entitled] Lulav va'Arava (Sukkah 46b) [the Gemara] said, "A person should not transfer ownership of a lulav to a child on the first day of Yom Tov, because a child can acquire, [but] cannot transfer ownership," and one cannot say that there [it is speaking] of a perceptive [minor], such as [one who is given] a pebble and throws it away, [or] a nut and takes it — for in the first chapter of Kiddushin (22b), in that incident where [the master] said to him, "Take off my shoe," it implies that he had understanding, and [yet] it says there, "Some say he was a minor"! One can answer that [a case where] another mind transfers ownership to them is different:

Tosafot on Gittin 39a:16:1.hebrew: וכי מי כתב גט שחרור לאלו - אלמא לא בעי גט להתירו בבת חורין, והיינו כשמואל דאמר: מי שאין לו רשות רבו עליו אינו קרוי עבד; וטעמא דאבא שאול בקטנים, דחשיב רשות רבן עליהן, כיון שאין להן יד בעצמן:
Tosafot on Gittin 39a:16:1.english: But who wrote a bill of manumission for these - Evidently, he does not require a bill [of manumission] to permit him [to marry] a free woman; and this is in accordance with Shmuel, who said: One who does not have his master's authority over him is not called a slave. And Abba Shaul's reason regarding minors [is] that their master's authority is considered [to be] over them, since they do not have legal capacity of their own:

Tosafot on Gittin 39a:17:1.hebrew: אלמה אמר אמימר כו' - וא"ת: מאי "אי הכי"? כ"ש דלשמואל תקשי דאמימר! וי"ל דהא לא קשיא ליה, משום דשמואל תנאי היא בפרק החולץ (יבמות מח.) ובפרק בתרא דנזיר (דף סב:); אבל הא קשיא ליה, אי אתיא דאמימר דלא כר' יוחנן רביה. ולהכי נמי לא מצי למיפרך לאמימר מדרבנן דאבא שאול, דאיהו מוקי להו כההוא תנא דאית ליה דשמואל, אבל איהו סבר כההוא תנא דפליג עלייהו, וסבר דלדידיה צריך גט שחרור ואין לו תקנה:
Tosafot on Gittin 39a:17:1.english: Why did Ameimar say, etc. - And if you ask: Why [did the Gemara say] "If so"? All the more so according to Shmuel, Ameimar's [statement] is difficult! And one can answer that this was not difficult for [the Gemara], because Shmuel's [view] is [a matter of] Tannaic dispute in the chapter [entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 48a) and in the last chapter of Nazir (62b); rather, this was difficult for [the Gemara]: whether Ameimar's [statement] does not accord with Rabbi Yoḥanan, his master. And for this reason as well, [the Gemara] could not raise an objection against Ameimar from the Rabbis [who dispute] Abba Shaul, for [Ameimar] establishes them as [holding] like that Tanna who holds like Shmuel, whereas [Ameimar himself] holds like that Tanna who disagrees with them, and holds that according to him a bill of manumission is required and [therefore] he has no remedy:

Tosafot on Gittin 39a:1:1.hebrew: הא מני ר"מ היא - הכא משמע דרב דלא כר"מ. והא דאמר בפ"ק דערכין (דף ה.): "האומר ערך כלי עלי, נותן דמיו", כר"מ, וכן בפ' האומר משקלי עלי (ערכין כ.) דתנן: "ערך ידי ורגלי עלי, לא אמר כלום", ואמר רב עלה: נותן דמיה, ומפרש לר"מ — אליבא דר"מ קאמר, וליה לא סבירא ליה. ואע"ג דבסוף פ"ק דסנהדרין (דף טו.), גבי "הערכין המטלטלין", מפרש רב באומר ערך כלי עלי כר"מ, לא סבירא ליה הכי. וכי האי גוונא אשכחן בריש אלמנה נזונית (כתובות דף צו.), דבעי למימר שמואל דהניזונת תנן וכאנשי יהודה, אע"ג דבסוף נערה שנתפתתה (כתובות נד.) אמר שמואל: הלכה כאנשי גליל:
Tosafot on Gittin 39a:1:1.english: Whose [opinion] is this? It is Rabbi Meir's - Here it implies that Rav does not [hold] like Rabbi Meir. And as for that which [Rav] said in the first chapter of Arakhin (5a): "[If] one says, 'The valuation of a vessel is upon me,' he gives its value," like Rabbi Meir, and similarly in the chapter [entitled] HaOmer Mishkali Alai (Arakhin 20a), where we learned [in the Mishnah]: "[If one says,] 'The valuation of my hand or my foot is upon me,' he has said nothing," and Rav said regarding it: "he gives its value," and [the Gemara] explains [that this is] according to Rabbi Meir — [Rav] spoke according to the opinion of Rabbi Meir, but he himself does not hold [so]. And even though at the end of the first chapter of Sanhedrin (15a), regarding "valuations [of] movable property," Rav explains [it as referring] to one who says, "The valuation of a vessel is upon me," like Rabbi Meir, he [himself] does not hold so. And like this we find at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Almana Nizonet (Ketubot 96a), where Shmuel wished to say that we learned [in the Mishnah] "ha-nizonet" ["who is supported"] and in accordance with the people of Judea, even though at the end of [the chapter entitled] Na'arah Shenitpatetah (Ketubot 54a), Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with the people of Galilee:

Tosafot on Gittin 39a:20:1.hebrew: הלכה כאבא שאול - אומר ר"ת דהלכה כריב"ל לגבי רבי יוחנן, כדמוכח בפרק בתרא דמגילה (דף כז.), דאמר: כוותיה דרב פפי מסתברא, דאמר ריב"ל, בית הכנסת מותר לעשותו בית המדרש; ואע"ג דר' יוחנן פליג עליה התם, דייק מדר' יהושע בן לוי דהלכה כרב פפי:
Tosafot on Gittin 39a:20:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Abba Shaul - Rabbeinu Tam says that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi against Rabbi Yoḥanan, as is proven in the last chapter of Megillah (27a), where [the Gemara] says: [The opinion] of Rav Pappi is more reasonable, for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, a synagogue may be turned into a study hall; and even though Rabbi Yoḥanan disagrees with him there, [the Gemara] infers from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi that the halakha is in accordance with Rav Pappi:

Tosafot on Gittin 39a:6:1.hebrew: עבדא כמקרקעי דמי - ולכך אין מועלים בו, דאין מעילה במחובר, דבפ' הנהנה (מעילה יח:) ילפינן מעילה "חטא" "חטא" מתרומה. והא דאמרי' בפ' המוכר את הספינה (ב"ב עט.): "הקדיש בור מלא מים, מועלין בו ובמה שבתוכו" — לא כמו שפי' שם רבינו שמואל, שהצניע חפציו בבור, דהא אין מעילה במחובר; אלא כשעקר מן הבור חוליא ונהנה ממנה:
Tosafot on Gittin 39a:6:1.english: A slave is considered equivalent to land - And therefore one does not commit me'ilah with him, for there is no me'ilah with attached [property], as in the chapter [entitled] Haneheneh (Me'ilah 18b) we derive me'ilah [via] "sin" [and] "sin" from terumah. And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Hamokher Et HaSefinah (Bava Batra 79a): "[If] one consecrated a cistern full of water, me'ilah applies to it and to what is inside it" — [this is] not as Rabbeinu Shmuel explained there, that he hid his possessions in the cistern, for there is no me'ilah with attached [property]; rather, [it refers to] when he detached a ring [of the lining] from the cistern and benefited from it:
